_: Trap kinds (2.10a, decision 0151 item 5): Morrowind's trapped-lock spells (world/sources/lore/topics/door-locks.md section Traps), each a packages/magic effects.json effect fired on whoever opens the trapped thing. magnitude: Morrowind's points range has no roll here, so the range's mean; durationSeconds as Morrowind; visualFamily is the effect's 2.9 family; trigger `open` (activating a still-trapped thing; a key or a probe disarms); probeThreshold the trap spell's cost (OpenMW's fTrapCostMult term, 0 in vanilla: see blockers); resets false (the spell is spent). A lock names its trap in locks.json `trap`. 2.9c-e adds `triggers` (step, tripwire, lever beside open and pick), `wiringKinds` (trap kinds the Teeth wiring fires: physical damage from the mined BladeTrap, HazardBase and TrapSwingingWall properties, spell damage from the mined flame spell and gas explosion), `nodes` (gates, barriers, pillars, markers) and `ignoredBases`; every number cites its mined field or the miner's gap value (world/sources/placement/traps-mined.json). `probeThresholdFrom` names the lock-trap row with the same effect (health damage for physical hits), its threshold being the one the existing probe check reads. `disarm.byProbe` is the existing probe check on the trigger; `byAvoidance` is a volume or lever the path never enters.
blockers: probeThreshold: world/76 section 118 Security row gives the pick check only; no passage gives a trap's difficulty in the no-dice check (Morrowind's is 0, fTrapCostMult); the spell cost is carried until one does
resets and the failed-pick trigger: UESP is silent (door-locks.md section Traps); one-shot on open is the dossier's inference

units: the mined damage numbers are Skyrim hit points (30..200 per hit), read against this game's stats pool unscaled; the first headless drive judges whether a unit map is owed (the owner rules retuning)

oneShot, resetS and triggerDelayS: Skyrim keeps them in the script body or Havok graph; the gap's nearest vanilla value is used where the property is a once-flag, resetS has no value in any gap (null), so a spent ref never re-arms

triggers.name: Open
triggers.rule: activating a still-trapped lock springs it; a key or a probe disarms (2.10a, locks.ts)

triggers.name: Failed pick
triggers.rule: an unprobed pick springs a pick-triggered trap (2.10a, locks.ts)

triggers.name: Step
triggers.rule: an actor not already inside the trigger volume enters it: fires the ref's targets once per entry. The volume is a local box (half extents or the base bounds) at the ref, turned by the ref's yaw and scaled by its scale. A ref with playerOnlyTrigger true counts only the one actor the user controls.
triggers.volumeFrom: mined primitive.boundsM (half extents, trigger boxes) else the base boundsUnits (a plate's phantom)
triggers.rawTypeProperty: TrapTriggerBase.TriggerType (3 on both Teeth trigger boxes; carried, the enum is in the script body)
sources: world/sources/placement/traps-mined.json cells.*.refs[].primitive, TrapTriggerBase and PressurePlate scripts

triggers.name: Tripwire
triggers.rule: an actor entering the wire's volume (the base bounds) springs it; it fires TriggerCount times and then is spent when FiniteUse. No Teeth cell carries one: the row is the vanilla base's own values.
sources: world/sources/placement/traps-mined.json bases Skyrim.esm:022F54 TrapTripwire01 Tripwire script

triggers.name: Lever
triggers.rule: activate(state, refId) throws the lever once: fires its targets through their activate-parent delays. A lever has no volume. The mined TrapLever script carries TriggerType 2.

wiringKinds.name: Swinging blade

damage.tierDerivation: Skyrim picks LvlDamageN by the level of the character who enters, set against LvlThresholdN. The world never receives a character level (docs/world/00-core.md rule 2), so no level indexes the table: the row is tier 1, Skyrim's own value for a character below LvlThreshold1, which is the arrival character that the Teeth's early route meets (King of the Murkmire quest stages 10 to 40, the defaultsetStageTrigSCRIPT triggers in the three cells). Every tier stays in `tiers` for a later fixed-danger rule.

wiringKinds.volumeFrom: base boundsUnits (the blade arm's swept box), scaled by the ref scale
